claims.statement: Polish law includes photovoltaic panels in WEEE group 4 and allows duties to be performed directly or through a recovery organization under written contract while producer responsibility remains.

A statutory recovery organization must be a producer-side joint-stock company with at least 5 million PLN fully paid in cash before registration; debt funding is prohibited, and ownership, reserves, environmental management, education, and audits are constrained by law.
EU law assigns producers financing responsibility for PV-panel collection and treatment, confirming recurring demand for compliant execution.
BDO reporting records producer contracts and collection, processing, recovery, and recycling mass flows.
ElektroEko, ELECTRO-SYSTEM, and TOM already sell the full compliance and treatment-network bundle to producers and importers.
At year-end 2025 Poland had 1,636,673 renewable microinstallations totaling nearly 13.9 GW, 99.9% photovoltaic, creating a large eventual installed base.
The frozen statutory collective cannot be bootstrapped with 65000 PLN or the founder's available 100000-200000 PLN because the non-debt paid-in legal floor is 5 million PLN.

contrary_evidence: The legal capital requirement directly invalidates the discovery-stage capital assumption.
Statutory ownership limits constrain founder-owned equity.
Multiple incumbents already provide the end-to-end duty-transfer bundle.
